gaps.text: In-line measurement of turbidity (optical state of the stream) with a turbidity or optical-density sensor at the measurement point
In-line measurement of temperature with a temperature sensor at the measurement point

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Fusion level: one model per method first, then joined variables scaled so that neither block dominates, because variables from different methods are not equivalent. The two probes must look at the same small whey volume and the data must be normalised to a common time step, which is harder for an ATR surface layer plus a bulk transmission path. The fused model must beat the best single method on independent runs, otherwise the second instrument is dropped.)
No supplied source reports protein quantification in whey by MIR-ATR or by NIR transmission; the dairy examples cover milk fat and protein and name whey filtration for NIR transmission.

items.finding: The source says temperature sensitivity of OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform the assessment by supporting temperature control or monitoring at the MIR ATR measurement point and by testing how temperature variation affects the aqueous whey spectra.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The statement is from a review and concerns aqueous solutions generally, not dairy whey or a specific in-line temperature sensor; transfer to a whey stream and probe configuration would need testing.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E01 ¶12

items.finding: The source says that before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
items.how_it_applies: This supports a staged fusion approach: first build one model per method, then check whether the second method adds complementary information before joining variables.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a review statement about data fusion generally, not a whey protein application, and it does not address scaling, common time steps, or ATR surface versus transmission path differences.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E03 ¶82

items.finding: In a rice authentication study, MIR alone gave better classification accuracy than NIR, while a SPORT-based multiblock fusion of MIR and NIR improved robustness.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform the assessment by supporting a test of MIR first and then MIR-NIR fusion, with the fused model compared against the best single method on independent runs.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The study is on rice authentication, not whey protein quantification, is available only as an abstract, and uses laboratory classification rather than in-line concentration measurement.

citation.quote: When analysed individually, MIR showed better predictive performance than NIR in terms of classification accuracy. The SPORT-based multiblock approach, integrating complementary MIR and NIR information, improved the exploitation of spectral variability and provided a more robust framework for modelling complex authenticity patterns.
citation.label: E04 ¶1
